transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I keep feeling like I’ve messed things up for everyone. Like I’m some kind of fake in my apprenticeship, and I’ve let my family down, and even the younger apprentices. It’s over stuff that, honestly, other people would probably just fix and move on from, but I can’t stop feeling guilty about it.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I don’t know if I’d call it depressed exactly. I’ve been feeling pretty low and guilty, yeah, but I’m not totally sure what counts as depressed.
Did these feelings start after a particular stressful event or setback?

Yeah, I think it started after I began the sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship. It’s been going on for about five months now, this whole pattern of feeling like I’m not keeping up or letting people down.
If the certification pressure were taken away, do you think these feelings would mostly go away?

I’m not really sure. I think it would help, because that’s been a big part of the pressure. But I don’t know if the guilt would just disappear. It kind of feels like it might still be there, just maybe less intense.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, not just the certification and apprenticeship?

I don’t think it’s across a bunch of different things, no. Mostly it circles back to the certification and work stuff. I mean, I worry about normal things too, but nothing that feels like it’s taking over everything.
For most of the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed nearly every day?
I’m not really sure I’d call it depressed nearly every day. I’ve felt off and weighed down at times, but I haven’t been tracking it day by day like that.
Have you been enjoying things less than you usually do?

Yeah, I think so. Lately I’ll walk past my sketchbook and just not feel like picking it up, or I’ll skip volleyball. I’ve also been ignoring messages from the volunteer group, even though those used to be things I actually looked forward to. Now I just don’t feel much about them.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt sad, empty, or down most of the day nearly every day?
I don’t know if I’d say most of the day nearly every day. I’ve had some down stretches, but I haven’t really been keeping track that closely.
Have you noticed your sleep has changed?

Yeah, it has. For a while I was only sleeping like three or four hours and still somehow showing up wired for work and class. But now it’s more like I can’t fall asleep, or I wake up before my alarm and feel like I didn’t rest at all.
During that time when you were sleeping only three or four hours, did you still feel unusually energetic?

Yeah. I felt kind of charged up, like I couldn’t really sit still. Even after a full day working on pipes, I’d still go to my evening class, then come home and reorganize all my tools, clean the apartment, or start drawing out systems instead of just relaxing.
During that time when you were sleeping only three or four hours, did you feel unusually confident or like you could handle more than other people?

Yeah… I did. I felt like I knew better than the instructors and even the senior guys at work. Like I could design a better system than them, and if people would just listen to me, I could change how buildings in Miami handled water. Looking back, that sounds like a lot, but at the time it felt true.
During that wired period, were you talking more than usual?

Yeah, I was. In class or at the shop, I’d start explaining some idea and then just keep going. I’d talk over people sometimes and barely stop to breathe, even when I could tell they were trying to move on or get back to work.
During that wired period, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?
I don’t really think so. I mean, I was more intense and doing more than usual, but I can’t think of anything actually risky or impulsive like that.
About how many days in a row did that wired period last?
It’s been going on for about five months altogether. It started after I began that sustainable plumbing certification on top of my apprenticeship.
During that wired period, did it cause major problems in your life, like at work, school, or in your relationships?

Yeah, it has started causing problems. My instructors and my foreman have had to keep after me about sketches I haven’t finished, and my work’s been slower than it should be. I’m honestly scared I’m getting close to messing up the apprenticeship and certification I worked really hard for.
During those five months, did that wired, unusually energized feeling stay there continuously the whole time?
Pretty much, yeah. It’s been this overall wired pattern for about five months now, since I started the sustainable plumbing certification along with my apprenticeship.
During that wired period, did you ever hear or see things that other people didn’t, or believe something others said wasn’t true?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been hearing or seeing things other people don’t, and I don’t think I’ve had beliefs like that.
During that wired period, were you ever hospitalized because of it?
No, I haven’t been hospitalized for it.
During that wired period, did it ever get so severe that you couldn’t function normally at work or school?

Yeah… not completely unable to function, but it’s definitely been affecting it. My instructors and my foreman have had to keep chasing me about unfinished sketches and my work being slower. I’m worried I’m getting close to messing up the apprenticeship and certification I worked really hard for.
